name: Peer review

subjectOf.text: Peer review exacerbates publication bias and can produce a cartelization of knowledge, because non-conforming innovative ideas may not receive full recognition and new findings that threaten existing hierarchies are delayed or denied recognition.
subjectOf.abstract: The use of peer reviews can further exacerbate these effects and can result in forms of cartelization of knowledge because non- conforming innovative ideas may not get full recognition.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization and Feedback Effects (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808852

subjectOf.text: Peer governance substitutes for platform gatekeeping: rather than convincing legacy technology leaders and their platforms, developer teams engage their own peers in the Shasper DAO to discuss and vote on proposed upgrades and testnet projects.
subjectOf.abstract: Rather than convincing legacy technology leaders and their respective platforms, teams of developers can engage directly with their own peers in the Shasper DAO to discuss and vote on proposed technology upgrades and Shasper testnet projects.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hybrid Secure Proof of Stake (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3931933

subjectOf.text: Community audits enable enhanced efficiency of coordination because voting associates, with their highly specialized philanthropic skillsets, are ideally positioned to identify other experts in philanthropy.
subjectOf.abstract: governance structure of the CHARITYxDAO enables enhanced efficiency of coordination because the VAs in the CHARITYxDAO, with their unique and highly specialized skillsets in the context of philanthropy, are ideally positioned to identify other experts in philanthropy.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Optimize Charitable Giving (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3981021
scope_conditions: DAOs whose members hold specialized philanthropic expertise

subjectOf.text: Multiple reviewers asking clarifying questions tends to make code simpler and clearer and therefore higher quality, but hierarchical review processes structurally block this mechanism.
subjectOf.abstract: the more people review the code with comments that ask for clarification, the more likely it becomes that the code becomes simpler and clearer, which in turn typically increases code quality. However, that is not possible in hierarchical review processes.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750
scope_conditions: code review settings that permit many independent reviewers

subjectOf.text: Gamification supplies quality control by making workers review and rate each other's contributions for points or recognition, which surfaces and resolves discrepancies through consensus-based voting or peer review rather than through duplicated independent work.
subjectOf.abstract: Gamification can be utilized to improve data quality through mechanisms like consensus-based voting or peer review. Workers can review and rate each other's contributions, earning points or recognition for accurate and consistent work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632

subjectOf.text: Model engines served as blind auditors of the design, the code and the text, and they are not independent peer review.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The description is the author's own, in the paper's byline footnote.
Sections IV and VI set out the audit rounds the footnote refers to.

subjectOf.text: Because the Gaussian outcomes already exist, written before any venue reviewed the design, the paper does not claim untouched Stage 1 status.
